registered_before: any E-pipeline run on AddBiomechanics data
question: Does the E criterion (contact-constrained GRF estimate and residual force from kinematics alone) reproduce force-plate GRF and contact on real human motion, and what residual force do real humans produce in it?
why: The 5% BW feasibility threshold and the residual-force estimator were never checked on human data; every E result and the RULA/REBA feasibility gate depend on them.

data.source: AddBiomechanics v1 (CC BY 4.0), With_Arm subset, train and test splits; 52 archive entries are empty upstream (8 in this subset)
data.pass: KINEMATICS (marker-based IK, no dynamic adjustment); sensitivity: DYNAMICS pass
data.joints_note: Spine3 and neck have no AddB joint; both are rigid on the torso (the acromial joints are torso-fixed in the Rajagopal skeleton) and the axial markers are registered per run, so they constrain the torso like the generated axial joints
data.frame_rate: resampled to 30 fps before the pipeline (generated inputs are 20-30 fps); sensitivity: native rate (about 100 Hz)
data.mass: DYNAMICS-pass skeleton mass for every pass and rate (AddB fits it to the force plates; the header mass can differ, e.g. 53.1 vs 48.9 kg, which would bias the vertical GRF by the same ratio without saying anything about the estimator); the header/DYNAMICS ratio is reported per trial

wholebody: Han2023 worrier, tree, treearms, chair, ballethighleg, taichi, soccerkick, tennisgroundstroke, tennisserve, step, dog, lambadadance, sidestretch, whirl

data.eligibility: trial length >= 2.0 s (1 s calibration and 0.5 s trims of the E pipeline leave >= 1 s); frames flagged unmeasuredExternalForceDetected or manualReview are excluded from every metric
data.selection: per class up to 24 trials, at most 4 per subject, uniform without replacement with numpy default_rng(20261105) over the sorted eligible list
data.known_at_registration: trial counts, lengths and GRF coverage per study (scan of the b3d headers); API checks on 9 trials: jointCenters equal the skeleton FK, Y-up world frame, groundContactForce equals the raw plate sum, header mass vs DYNAMICS mass; no E output had been computed

pipeline: biomech.prepare + biomech.dynamics exactly as for generated motion (scaling, axial registration, IK, 6 Hz filter, 100 Hz spline, required wrench, contact masks, NNLS GRF, residual); static optimization is not run

measured.grf: processing-pass groundContactForce of calcn_r and calcn_l (world frame, N), linearly interpolated to the pipeline times; frames whose AddB missingGRFReason is not notMissingGRF are excluded from GRF and contact metrics
measured.contact: per foot: measured vertical GRF > 20 N (约定，未经推演)

metrics.V1: total vertical GRF: per-trial Pearson r and RMSE in BW, estimated vs measured
metrics.V2: total horizontal GRF magnitude: per-trial Pearson r and RMSE in BW
metrics.V3: per-foot contact: balanced accuracy of the pipeline mask (heel or toe) against measured contact
metrics.V4: residual force per frame (BW) after the 0.5 s trims: distribution per class; per-trial residual RMS and share of frames above 0.05 BW
metrics.summary: per class: median and interquartile range over trials; pooled human statistics weight classes equally

threshold.frame: tau_frame = 99th percentile of per-frame residual (BW) over the human frames of stand, walk, run, squat, jump and wholebody (classes weighted equally); sts is reported but excluded because the seat supports the pelvis and the pipeline models foot contact only
threshold.run: tau_run = 95th percentile of per-trial residual RMS over the same classes
threshold.use: post hoc sensitivity on X3/E4/E1/ARDY-fair: feasibility and RULA/REBA gate recomputed with tau_frame in place of 0.05 BW; registered for X4 as the feasibility threshold if the gate passes

gate.pass_if: walk and run: median V1 r >= 0.9 and median V1 RMSE <= 0.15 BW; median V3 balanced accuracy >= 0.85 in walk, run and jump (约定，未经推演)
gate.fail: X4 runs generation only; the E criterion waits for an estimator fix, which is registered before it is evaluated on these trials
